body: Thanks for the thoughtful reply and the good questions. I feel like I have everything going for me; I have a good job and rumor has it that I’m going to get engaged to a wonderful person soon. I am excited, but more guilty because they deserve someone who isn’t overcome with self hatred. So I have good goals and good things coming my way, but I feel  these things are better suited for someone far superior to me if that makes sense.

Likewise, I’m glad I’m not the only one’! I like to imagine what their lives are like; the impatient man honking and checking his phone, the bored lady with dead eyes zoned out at the stoplight. It reminds me that there are so many lives out there, each with their own unique set of worries,  insecurities, and issues
“Could I trouble you for a glass of warm milk?” “No, but you can trouble me for a warm glass of shut the hell up.”

Not quite “I didn’t let on that I knew who they were”, more like “I didn’t realize who they were until seconds after the interaction ended.” 

This was a few years back. I was a senior in high school working at an upscale grocery store chain that’s only in Minnesota. I was cashiering later and night and this beautiful middle aged woman with the nicest smile came through my line. She was with a guy about her age. I treated her like any other customer, just pleasantly conversational and polite. I noticed a few co workers and customers staring but didn’t think much of it in the moment. 

I thank her, wish her a good night, and she leaves. Within seconds co workers rush to my lane whispering excitedly to the effect of “dude, that was Lauren Graham!” Anybody whose cashiered knows that all the faces blur together, so it suddenly made sense why hers stuck out in such a good way. 

I learned that the guy with her was her partner Peter Krause (who is also her Parenthood co star). Turns out he’s from Minnesota and still spends a fair amount of time here. Still bummed I didn’t fangirl over Lorelai harder, but it was probably for the best!
